title: AgentPoolProperties
description: Properties for the container service agent pool profile.

provisioningState.description: The current deployment or provisioning state.

count.description: Number of agents (VMs) to host docker containers. Allowed values must be in the range of 0 to 1000 (inclusive) for user pools and in the range of 1 to 1000 (inclusive) for system pools. The default value is 1.

vmSize.description: The size of the agent VMs.

maxPods.description: The maximum number of pods that can run on a node.

osSKU.description: Specifies the OS SKU used by the agent pool.

mode.description: A cluster must have at least one System agent pool at all times.

orchestratorVersion.description: The version of Kubernetes running on the Agent Pool.

currentOrchestratorVersion.description: The running Kubernetes version on the Agent Pool.

minCount.description: The minimum number of nodes for auto-scaling.

maxCount.description: The maximum number of nodes for auto-scaling.

scaleSetPriority.description: The Virtual Machine Scale Set priority.

scaleSetEvictionPolicy.description: The Virtual Machine Scale Set eviction policy.

spotMaxPrice.description: The maximum price for spot instances.

scaleDownMode.description: Describes how VMs are added to or removed from Agent Pools.

vnetSubnetID.description: The ID of the subnet for agent pool nodes.

podSubnetID.description: The ID of the subnet for pods.

enableNodePublicIP.description: Whether each node gets its own public IP.

nodePublicIPPrefixID.description: The public IP prefix ID for the nodes.

nodeLabels.description: The node labels to be persisted across all nodes.

nodeTaints.description: The taints added to new nodes.

tags.description: The tags to persist on the VMSS.

proximityPlacementGroupID.description: The ID for Proximity Placement Group.

availabilityZones.description: The list of Availability zones to use for nodes.

workloadRuntime.description: The type of workload a node can run.

messageOfTheDay.description: A base64-encoded message of the day for Linux nodes.
